reader_notes: Format observation, not a prose complaint: this is a five-gap cloze, whereas the ELF units I came in expecting are texts followed by comprehension questions. The writing itself reads as genuine British column prose.

Gaps 1 and 2 are idiom recall (“spares nobody’s feelings”, “short shrift”) rather than contextual reasoning; gaps 3 and 5 do reward reading the surrounding argument, and gap 3’s phonetic set (interference / deference / inference / indifference) is tight, with only one option that the following two sentences support.
The churchyard card staying up “all summer” only squares with the stated first-Monday rule if that card carries a date. The text lets you infer it, but it took a beat.
The piano-lessons card at the end is a deliberate exception to the rule and is presented as such, so it reads as the essay’s punchline rather than as a contradiction.
